# Further reading {#sec-logistic-inference-reading}

- [Hua Zhou](https://hua-zhou.github.io/)'s [course page for "UCLA Biostat 257 - Statistical Computing" (2025 Spring)](https://ucla-biostat-257.github.io/2025spring/)
  has lectures on fitting generalized linear models and on quasi-Newton optimization.
  Its source is [on GitHub](https://github.com/ucla-biostat-257/2025spring) under the MIT License.
- David Rocke's EPI 204 lecture
  [*Logistic Regression and Likelihood*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-01.mp4)
  ([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2%20Logistic%20Regression%20and%20Likelihood.pdf))
  fits [logistic regression](#def-logistic-regression) by [maximum likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle)
  and compares models by [deviance](#def-deviance) and [AIC](model-validation.qmd#def-aic)
  [@rocke2021epi204].
- Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
  [*Logistic Regression Details Pt 2: Maximum Likelihood*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BfKanl1aSG0)
  shows how [maximum likelihood estimation](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle) fits a logistic regression curve
  [@starmer2018logistic].
